summary: Vegetarian street-style tacos of tofu and zucchini grilled with achiote oil and cut into dice, mixed with sauteed onion, garlic and bell peppers, and served on warm corn tortillas with guacamole and grilled pineapple salsa; serves 4.
glance: 1.5 ounces achiote paste mashed into 1/2 cup canola oil, with cumin, hot sauce and salt
10 ounces extra-firm, cut in 1/3-inch slabs and grilled
faq: What is achiote?

Achiote, also called annatto, is the typical coloring that gives cheddar cheese its orange tint. The easiest way to cook with it is a preground box, which comes as a slightly moist little brick, because the whole seeds aren't always easy to find.
Which achiote brand is good?
The author likes El Yucateco because it doesn't have or need synthetic food coloring added.
How do you make the achiote oil?
Break up the achiote paste with a fork and mash in 1/2 cup canola oil a little at a time until it dissolves, then mix in cumin, hot sauce and salt.
How do you grill the tofu?
Brush the tofu slabs (patted dry) with achiote oil on one side and grill on a medium flame until well marked, brush the other side, flip and grill. Do the same with zucchini, then cool and dice both.
How do you warm the tortillas?
Wrap in a damp, clean dish towel and microwave about 3 minutes until soft and warm. Use two tortillas per taco.
What goes with these tacos?
Guacamole, grilled pineapple salsa and extra hot sauce. The secret to this kind of Mexican food is amped-up flavor and contrasting textures.

summary: Young coconut salad: tender, custard-like young coconut halves served in their shells with watercress, pomegranate arils, lime juice and flaky sea salt, with the coconut water on the side; serves 4.
glance: 2 young coconuts (not mature brown-husked ones), kept refrigerated until serving
faq: What is a young coconut?

Very different from the mature brown-husked kind: the interior flesh is tender, thin and custard-like, with the purest coconut flavor imaginable. Find them at Asian markets or health-food stores that cater to raw foodists.
How should I store young coconuts?
Keep them refrigerated until just before serving.
How do I stop the cut coconut from discoloring?
Immediately rub the cut shell surface with a lime half after cutting the coconut in half lengthwise.
What can I use instead of watercress?
Any other small, flavorful green such as mache or arugula.
What do I do with the coconut water?
Reserve it when you open the tops and serve it in a glass on the side. If you have a seltzer bottle or whipped cream maker with seltzer cartridges, you can carbonate it for extra fun.

summary: Corned beets: thin-sliced beets cooked in a salty spiced brine (sous vide at 85°C for about 1 hour 20 minutes, or simmered), dehydrated at 145°F for about 4 hours, then rehydrated to a chewy, cured-meat-like texture; yields 350 grams.
glance: 350 grams, enough for at least 3 good-sized sandwiches
Prep 20 min, cook 6 hrs, total 6 hrs 20 min
brine, cook, dehydrate, rehydrate; stovetop and oven version is untested
faq: What are corned beets?
Beets cooked with the spices typically associated with corned beef, which began as a pun. The texture is what makes them delightful: completely cooked, with a satisfying chew.
Why dehydrate and then rehydrate the beets?

The beets are cooked in the brine, then dehydrated, and then rehydrated. The first test dehydrated too long and turned into dry, salty chips; rehydrating washed away the excess salt and left a nice bite from the spices and an awesome texture.
Can I make corned beets without special equipment?

The author has only made them sous vide with a dehydrator and a chamber vacuum, but expects you can simmer them in a pot, dry them in a low oven (about 170°F, around 2 hours, with convection) and rehydrate them in a covered bowl in the refrigerator, checking every half-hour. It is untested.
What spice mix should I use?
The ChefSteps House Rub 01 (smaller amounts of salt and spice mix) or the spice mix from Elise's corned beef recipe (larger amounts).
How do I serve corned beets?

On a simple sandwich of toasted rye or pumpernickel with mayo and strong mustard, or dressed up with pumpernickel, sour cream, pickled shallot, capers and watercress. Include something with acidic punch to play against the earthiness.

summary: Greek green bean salad for a potluck: 2 1/2 pounds of green beans blanched (or cooked sous vide at 85°C for 15 minutes) and shocked in ice water, held cold up to a day, then dressed with olive oil, creamy feta, black olives and fresh marjoram.
glance: Prep 10 min, cook 15 min, total 25 min
hold the beans cold a day in advance and dress close to serving
lots of fresh marjoram, or fresh oregano and/or thyme
faq: Can I make Greek green bean salad ahead?
Yes. The beans are blanched and shocked and you can hold them cold a day in advance, then dress them close to serving time. Toss just before serving, since it looks beautiful before tossing.
How do you cook the green beans?

Either boil them in a very large pot of salted water until just barely tender and still bright green, in two batches if necessary, or seal them in a bag with the olive oil and salt and cook sous vide at 85°C for 15 minutes. Shock in an ice bath either way.
What is marjoram and what can I use instead?

Marjoram is in the same family as oregano, with a flavor the author finds more complex and resinous. It is especially loved in Greek cuisine and pairs beautifully with feta and olives. If you can't find fresh, use fresh oregano and/or thyme.
What feta and olives should I buy?
The best you can afford, because the dish is so simple. The author used creamy feta and pitted Taggiasca black olives.
Any ways to add flavor?
Add a bit of lemon or orange zest.

summary: A review of Amy Sedaris's I Like You: Hospitality Under the Influence, with a recipe for Greek koulourakia cookie twists with cardamom: butter, sugar and cream dough rolled into 7-inch ropes, twisted, brushed with egg white and sesame seeds and baked at 350°F for 25 minutes.
glance: I Like You: Hospitality Under the Influence by Amy Sedaris
350°F for 25 minutes or until light brown
like a sable cookie, a bit fluffier than biscocos, with a hit of cardamom
faq: Is I Like You a joke cookbook?

Your first impression might be that it is, with hilarious photos on nearly every page, but the author says virtually every one of the hundreds of recipes is legitimate, edible and often delicious, especially the Greek recipes from the Sedaris family heritage.
Who should buy I Like You?

The author says yes if you already think Amy Sedaris or her brother David are hilarious, grew up in the 1960s or 70s or are fascinated by them, love kitschy American food, or long for the days of a shag-carpet basement.
How is the book organized?

After introductory remarks on the art of hospitality, short chapters based on entertaining scenarios such as Entertaining the Elderly, Ladies' Night and Lumberjack Brunch, with practical advice such as a chart of guest combinations to avoid.
What are koulourakia?
Greek cookie twists. This recipe, similar to the author's family biscocos but fluffier and with cardamom, is reminiscent of a sable cookie and very nice with coffee.
How do you shape koulourakia?
Roll a tablespoon or two of dough into a 7-inch rope, fold the rope in half and twist, place on a foil-lined sheet, brush with egg whites and top with sesame seeds.
